evidence.description: Lists the sources that prove the claim. Someone who doubts the claim must be able to open or rerun each one and see the same thing.

ref.description: Names what to open or rerun, such as a file:line range, a command, a commit, a sentence of the goal, or a documentation URL.

shows.description: States what the source shows, quoting the code or the output that matters.

basis.description: Says whether you ran the command or only read the source.

verdict.description: Is approve when no blocker or major finding remains, and revise otherwise.

summary.description: Summarizes the review in one or two sentences.

findings.description: Lists proven problems in the change itself. Every finding lies inside the change's scope.

id.description: Holds a stable id such as F1 or F2. The same issue keeps the same id across turns.

category.description: Classifies the finding. A scope finding means the change touches code the goal does not require, and its fix is to revert that code.

location.description: Names the file path and line range in the working tree, such as src/auth/session.ts:41-58.

issue.description: States what is wrong, quantified where possible.

fix.description: Describes the minimal change that resolves the finding inside the change's scope.

preExisting.description: Lists problems noticed in code the change does not touch. They are informational and never become findings.

location.description: Names the file path and line range.

issue.description: States the problem in one sentence.
